thread.title: Why Is Apple Giving Away Free Original Content To Device Owners?

author: investopedia.com
title: Why Is Apple Giving Away Free Original Content To Device Owners?
text:
Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) is making a fresh attempt at reinventing TV on its platform.
According to a CNBC report , the Cupertino company will insert a “pre-installed” service in the TV application on its hardware devices, such as iPad, iPhone, and Apple TV. The service will contain a mix of programming, from original content produced by Apple to subscriptions for popular streaming apps from content providers, such as HBO and Starz. The idea behind the service is to enable a single-stop shop for content consumers, who would, otherwise, have to navigate to multiple apps in order to watch individual programming.
The Cupertino company is planning to spend $1 billion on original content this year and is reported to have signed on big names – Steven Spielberg, Oprah Winfrey, Reese Witherspoon – to star in or direct shows for its service. According to a WSJ story in April, Apple is positioning itself as a family-friendly service and avoiding the edgy content generally favored by other streaming services.
Reports last year had indicated that the company might charge $15 for its service, but the CNBC report states that Apple-owned content will be free. The world’s biggest streaming service Netflix Inc. ( NFLX ) has a tiered approach to pricing with a range between $7.99 to $13.99. Amazon.com Inc. (A MZN ), which has a service similar to the one being planned by Apple, offers it for free to its Amazon Prime subscribers. (See also: Apple Considers Streaming TV Bundle ).
Apple’s has had plans to start a TV service on its hardware platform for at least a decade. But those plans have run into problems due to hesitation from content providers afraid to commit to such a service. The tech behemoth is largely blamed for the decline in revenues in the music industry after it unbundled lucrative music albums into individual songs costing $0.99 each. A similar approach to television would sound the death knell for large studios, who produce a variety of shows for multiple cable networks.
The Right Approach Apple’s efforts to build out and generate revenues from its TV service is part of a broader move towards transitioning to a services company. In recent earnings calls, Apple CEO Tim Cook has touted the increasing share of services revenue on Apple’s income statement.
Analysts have lauded Apple’s move. According to Gene Munster from Loup Ventures, it is the “ right approach ” for the company. He provided four reasons for his assessment. First, Apple’s move will build awareness of its video content with 1 billion users of its hardware devices. Second, it will attract and retain more users onto its hardware platforms. Third, it will drive the usage of the TV app. Finally, a “loyal viewer base” for its television content will also enable Apple to sell paid options and other products and bring in more revenues for its services segment.
